How to Size a Transfer Switch

Choosing the correct transfer switch size is crucial for safe and effective backup power. Here's what you need to consider:

Match Your Generator Output

Your transfer switch should match your generator's output capacity. A common formula:

  • Watts ÷ Volts = Amps
  • Example: 7,500W ÷ 240V = 31.25A → Use a 30A transfer switch

Consider Your Electrical Panel

The transfer switch should not exceed your main panel's capacity. Most homes have 100A, 150A, or 200A service.

Common Transfer Switch Sizes

Switch Size Generator Range Typical Use
30 Amp 5,000 - 7,500W Portable generators, essential circuits
50 Amp 10,000 - 12,000W Large portable or small standby generators
100 Amp 15,000 - 22,000W Whole-house standby generators
200 Amp 22,000W+ Large homes, service entrance rated
